title: Webhook delivery: at least once, without waiting on merchants
brief: Design webhook delivery: your platform emits events and must POST each one to the merchant's endpoint, at least once. Merchant endpoints are slow: model them as one Service block with capacity_rps 100000, base_latency_ms 400, timeout_ms 30000. A worker delivers about 200 events/s.

requirements: Emitting an event p99 < 300 ms: the API must not wait on merchants
variants.twist: Deliveries stop for 30 s: kill_node on your worker block, then restore_node. Does the backlog drain? In production, how do you keep one dead endpoint from blocking everyone else (retry queue with backoff, dead-letter queue)?

requirements: Emitting p99 < 300 ms, errors < 0.1%, backlog under 1,000
Events for one merchant must arrive in order
variants.twist: One merchant gets 30% of all events. With ordering per merchant, all of them land on one partition. What does that do to that merchant's lag, and to everyone else's?

hints: Should the API that emits an event wait for the merchant to answer?

Put a queue between the API and delivery workers, then size the workers to drain faster than events arrive. At 12k/s: what is your queue's intake limit, and what does a per-message price come to per hour?

Steady: service -> queue -> about 11 workers -> merchants. Black Friday: about 15 services -> Kafka with about 66 partitions -> 66 workers (one reader per partition; key by merchant for ordering). SQS also works but costs about $50/hr in requests.
_notes: Workers 200/s, $0.10. Steady: sync (service -> merchants) gives p99 ~520 ms and 0.8% errors. Queue ($0.05, 3k/s) + 9 workers: rho 1.1, backlog fills; 11 workers: p99 ~36 ms, $1.55; 20 workers ($2.45) break the budget. Black Friday: one queue rejects above 3k/s (79% errors). SQS: $60/hr in requests. Kafka ($0.63) with 12 partitions and 65 workers: only 12 read, backlog explodes. Kafka 66 partitions + 66 workers + 15 services: p99 ~36 ms, $8.83; a generic Stream with 66 partitions is cheaper. The sim doesn't model failed deliveries staying in the queue or per-merchant isolation; cover retries, backoff with jitter, DLQ and signing in the postmortem. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
